text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey was forced to ask for foreign help in order to extinguish a fire at a munitions factory in Kirikkale, despite successive ministers having promised to buy the right equipment.
- A police intelligence chief accused of organisng infiltration and surveillance of the armed forces will be charged with treason.
- A military appeal court overturned a 30-day sentence on a naval official accused of passing on information to police intelligence, saying it was insufficient.
- Former foreign minister, Tansu Ciller has said she did not know about the police surveillence operation on the army, but that it was conducted on the initiative of the police officers.
- Senior MPs in Ciller's True Path Party are unhappy with Ciller's leadership which could lead to further resignations from her party next week.
- The previous Islamist-led government had removed senior officials at the Kirikkale munitions factory, replacing them with supporters who did not have any knowledge of the industry.
- The paper asks who was responsible for the explosions at the munitions plant at Kirikkale and who will take responsibility for investigating the blasts.
